description: We are a creative team passionate about space, science, and storytelling. Our goal is to bring forgotten space missions to life through engaging and meaningful stories. We welcome curious minds who love creativity, teamwork, and learning. We are looking for storytellers, writers, researchers, designers, web developers, animators, and video editors. All skill levels are welcome!
summary:
The Stars Remember is an interactive educational project that brings forgotten space exploration equipment back into the spotlight. Across the Moon and Mars, many machines and spacecraft components have completed their missions and remain on the surfaces of these worlds. Instead of treating them as abandoned objects, our project gives them a voice through creative storytelling supported by real space science.

Through an interactive digital experience, visitors can explore historic missions, discover the stories behind these machines, and learn about their scientific and engineering achievements. By combining space exploration, technology, and storytelling, The Stars Remember transforms space history into an engaging learning experience and reminds people that every machine has a story worth remembering.
details: The Stars Remember is an interactive digital experience designed to make the history of space exploration more accessible, engaging, and memorable. Our project focuses on the legacy of space equipment left behind after completing important missions on the Moon and Mars. It transforms these machines into storytelling characters, allowing visitors to discover their journeys, purposes, challenges, and contributions to space exploration. The website features an interactive space-themed experience with mission stories, historical information, educational content, and activities that encourage visitors to explore and learn. It includes information about missions and equipment such as Surveyor, Apollo lunar modules, Sojourner, Opportunity, and InSight. Our main goal is to connect science with storytelling. By presenting real historical facts through creative and accessible digital content, we aim to inspire curiosity about astronomy, robotics, engineering, and the future of space exploration. The project was developed using web technologies, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and hosted on Vercel. We focused on creating an accessible, engaging, and responsive experience that combines educational value with creativity and interactive learning. What makes The Stars Remember unique is its perspective: instead of focusing only on successful missions and famous astronauts, it tells the stories of the machines that helped make those achievements possible. We believe that even after a mission ends, its contribution should never be forgotten.
